name: 2123 Prairie Avenue — brick house with a brownstone front, a stone bow and a slated mansard, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). No building date or loss date is read for it (T-3724).

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body at its north wall: column 1033.5, row 1304.5 of sheet 35 at full size (T-3724), 2.2 m behind and 1.3 m north of the draft's corner (the draft's fit had read a 15.25 m deep, 5.75 m wide block), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading. Rotation 179.318 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2123 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2123 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: 21.47 m from the rear wall (column 1033.5) to the stone front (column 918, the outer edge of the blue band, as 2115's is read), and 9.48 m along the front from the north wall (row 1304.5) to the south wall (row 1355.5), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3724) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel). The draft's fit drew it 15.25 by 5.75 m. Not built (liberty L-k01-2123-prairie-3724): the south wall's 1.2 m step in over the rear 5.6 m (row 1349 from column 1003), and the front's south-west corner cut back 1.9 m round the entrance (rows 1343-1355.5 to column 928).

stories.note: The 1911 sheet prints '3B' on the main body: three storeys over a basement, the third in the mansard (the key's dashed mansard line runs inside the whole outline). The Armour photograph shows the front's two full storeys under a slated mansard (x 1720-2000, y 290-1030 px), so K01 stands two walled storeys and the roof storey.

construction.note: The sheet draws the main body pink (brick) with a blue band (the key's stone front) along the street front, bowed out over its north half.

stone_front.note: The sheet's blue band makes the front stone. The Armour photograph shows it far darker than 2115's pale limestone beside it in the same light (x 1720-2000 px against x 820-1530), and smooth, with dressed mouldings round the lights: read as brown sandstone, the dark stone of the avenue's fronts of the 1870s. Which quarry cannot be read off a halftone. T-3725: the rusticated base runs four courses (0.44 m each) up to the basement lights' heads, 2.0 m over grade as the camera reads them.

principal_floor_m.note: The photograph's basement storey, read through the T-3725 camera on the Armour photograph (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json, about 58.5 px a metre at this front, the eye 1.6 m over grade): the principal lights' sills stand 2.88 m over grade (y 1015 px), so the floor at 2.55 m under the record's 0.3 m sill. T-3724 had 1.8 m, read at an assumed 65 px a metre; the garden kerb hides the grade itself, so the grade is the camera's (the eye's height under its horizon).

storey_heights_m.note: Read through the T-3725 camera on the Armour photograph (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json, about 58.5 px a metre at this front, the eye 1.6 m over grade): the principal and chamber lights' sills at 2.88 and 7.39 m (y 1015 and 752 px), a storey of 4.5 m; the cornice's frieze, blocks and corona standing over the chamber lights' heads as the print draws them (the corona's top at about y 506 px, the frieze's foot at about y 575), so the chamber storey 4.6 m to the wall head, as 2115's beside it is 4.5 m. T-3724's 4.0 and 3.8 m stood the cornice about 2 m low against the picture.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as every K01 stone front.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

face_brick.note: The flanks and rear are brick (the sheet's pink). The photograph shows the north flank as dark as the stone front, plain and unlit where it shows over 2115's south piece (x 1555-1720, y 320-700 px): K03's salmon common brick, the darkest common brick the kit lays, against 2115's pale buff.

street_front_trim.note: K01's flat lintel under each storey's round heads, as 2115's (the round heads are below).

street_front_round_heads.note: Every front light the photograph shows is round-headed, in both storeys (x 1750-1980, y 620-1030 px), each under a moulded hood with a key.

wall_head.note: The photograph shows a deep cornice on blocks over a plain frieze across the front, carried round the north flank (x 1555-2000, y 510-565 px), as 2115's. K10's moulded stone cornice with its blocks; the rear is carried the same (no picture of it).

roof_form.note: The sheet's dashed line inside the whole main body's outline is the key's mansard roof, and the photograph shows the slated mansard with its deck's iron cresting.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall, as 2115's: no picture looks down on it.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's reach in the photograph, a little short of 2115's.

mansard.note: Off the photograph: a straight-faced slated mansard about 3 m high (y 320-510 px), two round-headed dormers on the street face over the bow and the light beside it (x 1840-1865 and 1915-1950, y 400-490 px), one on the north flank part way back (x 1580-1615, y 425-470 px; K01 names that face 'south', the house being turned to front west), and iron cresting with small finials round the deck (y 290-320 px). The photograph stops short of the door's end of the front, so no third street dormer is built; how many more stand on the north flank behind the one it shows cannot be read. The deck's 0.5 m cresting is the kit's. T-3725, through the T-3725 camera on the Armour photograph (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json): the mansard rises 3.5 m from the cornice to the deck's curb (the curb at y about 322 px, about 15.2 m over grade over the 11.65 m wall head; T-3724's 3.0 m on a 9.6 m wall stood it about 140 px low), and the two street dormers stand 3.6 and 5.5 m along the front (x about 1855 and 1935 px; T-3724 had 2.8 and 5.75 m, which this camera draws 30-70 px south of the print's): over the bow's south half and over the light beside it. The slate over the bow's middle is plain in the print. The north flank's one dormer (K01's 'south' face; x 1580-1615 px) stands 18.9 m from the rear wall, 2.6 m behind the front, through the same camera (T-3724 had 11.0 m, which this camera hides behind 2115).

roof_covering.note: The photograph's mansard faces read as slate, darker than 2115's banded faces and plain; the deck, unseen, is tin as 2115's.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: Held short so the flight stays inside the sheet's entrance corner.

stoop_width_m.note: The sheet's entrance corner is 2.4 m wide (rows 1343-1355.5); the stoop is held inside it.

entrance_bay.note: The door stands in the front's south bay, where the sheet cuts the front's south-west corner back (rows 1343-1355.5, to column 928): the bay the photograph does not reach. The draft had read the same side.

front_bays.note: Bay centres from the north corner (K01's 'south to north', the house turned to front west): the single round-headed light beside the bow (photograph x 1920-1980 px, 5.75 m by the sheet's bow ending at row 1330), and the door's bay at 8.3 m, the middle of the sheet's entrance corner (rows 1343-1355.5). The bow's own lights are on the bay below.

side_bays.note: K01's 'south' wall is this house's north flank: the photograph shows it plain where it rises over 2115's south piece (x 1555-1720 px) and the sheet's frame bay stands on it lower down, so it is laid with no lights of its own.

north_bays.note: The south flank (K01's 'north' wall, metres from the front): no picture shows it. Three lights a storey along the 2.4 m side passage, clear of the entrance corner.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall beside the range (K01 counts it from the south): one light a storey on the 2.8 m the range leaves clear at the north end; no picture shows it.

sash_by_storey.note: The photograph's front lights, about 1.0 m wide, read through the T-3725 camera on the Armour photograph (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json, about 58.5 px a metre at this front, the eye 1.6 m over grade): 2.6 m tall in the principal storey (y 860-1015 px, 2.66 m) and 2.4 m in the chamber storey (y 610-752 px, 2.43 m; T-3724 had 2.2), sills low to the floor.

basement_lights.note: The photograph's square-headed basement openings between stone piers (y 1060-1150 px): read through the T-3725 camera on the Armour photograph (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json, about 58.5 px a metre at this front, the eye 1.6 m over grade), 0.57 to 2.11 m over grade, so a 1.45 m light on a 0.55 m sill (T-3724's 0.9 m light was read at an assumed scale).

window_kit.note: K06's two-over-two sash; the round-headed lights take its round fanlight sash, as 2115's.

rainwater.note: The kit's copper gutter behind the cornice, one downpipe at the rear: the photograph shows none on the front.

chimneys.note: The photograph shows one tall brick stack on the north wall (x 1545-1610, top y 252 px). Through the T-3725 camera (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json) it stands on the deck just inside the north curb (1.6 m in from the north wall; K01 refuses a stack astride the curb) at 16.75 m from the rear wall, 4.7 m behind the front, and its top 17.4 m over grade, about 2.1 m over the deck (T-3724 had placed it 7.5 m from the rear at 1.6 m, read at an assumed scale). Its partner on the south wall is reconstructed (no picture shows that side) and keeps T-3724's 7.5 m from the rear, drawn 1.1 m in from the south wall so the taller mansard's curb clears it; both share the kit's one height over the deck.

entrance_kit.note: The front stands 7.43 m behind the street line (column 918 against the line at 878), on 2115's front line. The door is not in the photograph; it is laid round-arched like every opening the photograph shows on this front, a pair of leaves under a fanlight, deep in the stone. T-3725: the arch's keystone top is carried up with the principal floor (1.8 to 2.55 m), 6.0 m over grade.

boundary.note: The photograph shows the yard open to the walk behind a low stone kerb, as 2115's (x 1500-2000, y 1180-1230 px); the lot runs from row 1301.6 to row 1368.8.

yard.note: The photograph's yard, snow over bare beds behind the kerb (y 1150-1230 px); the walk to the door is the kit's flags, as 2115's.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the bow's pair of round-headed principal lights in the Armour photograph (x 1760-1890, y 860-1030 px)
the bow's pair of square-headed basement lights between stone piers under its principal lights in the Armour photograph (x 1765-1830 and 1875-1935, y 1060-1150 px)
the bow's pair of round-headed chamber lights in the Armour photograph (x 1750-1880, y 610-752 px), the bow's top held under the cornice's bed

bays.note: The sheet's stone bow: the blue band bowed out to column 912-913 over rows 1309-1330, 0.93 m proud of the front over a 3.9 m chord centred 2.79 m from the north wall; the photograph shows its pair of round-headed lights in both storeys. The sheet's frame bay on the north flank (yellow, columns 950-966, 3.0 m long, about 0.55 m out, no storey count) is not built: K08 cuts no light in a bay that shallow and refuses one without (liberty L-k01-2123-prairie-3724). T-3725: the bow's storeys follow the house's (7.05 m to the chamber floor, its top 0.3 m under the 11.65 m wall head), its basement carries the print's two square-headed lights under its principal pair, and its chamber lights are 2.4 m, as read through the T-3725 camera on the Armour photograph (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/chicagology_armour_photo.json, about 58.5 px a metre at this front, the eye 1.6 m over grade).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's pink '2B' rear range, columns 1033.5-1070, rows 1320-1355.5: 6.78 m deep and 6.69 m wide, its south wall on the main body's. Two storeys over the basement; heights, lights and its tin deck are reconstructed.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling with a stone front (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: 2115 S. Prairie (Armour mansion). Photograph of the Philip D. Armour house's street front and north flank, taken from the west walk of Prairie Avenue in winter, with the south end of 2109 (the Roloson house) at its left edge and 2117 at its right; unknown photographer, undated. Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2115 S. Prairie.
what_it_supplies: the front's south end: the second storey's round-headed light and its hood, the corner pilaster strip, the frieze and the bracketed cornice
the mansard over the front, its round-headed dormer and scrolled surround, the deck's cornice and the stack
the veranda: its columns, pedestals, balustrade, entablature and flat roof, its run across the front and down the south side, its floor's height and the open piers under it
the rear block's cornice standing at the front's height beyond the veranda
what_it_does_not_supply: the front's north part (out of the frame), the north flank, the rear and the back porches

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-3724 (piece 2 of T-1930, the S18 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K03 brick body behind a brown sandstone front, K06 round-headed sash, a K07 round-arched double door and stoop, a K08 stone bow and frame side bay, a K10 moulded cornice, a K05 slated mansard with dormers and the deck's iron cresting, and the attached two-storey rear range — instead of the draft builder. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size ('3B', brick with a stone front bowed over its north half, the key's dashed mansard line round the whole body, the entrance corner cut back at the south-west, a small frame bay on the north flank, the '2B' rear range) and the Armour photograph (data/sources/chicagology_2115_armour_photo.json), whose right edge shows the north half of this front and its north flank. T-3725 solved the photograph's camera on this house and re-read its heights, dormers and stack through it (data/reference_views/house_2123_prairie/); the image-gate sign-off waits on the two differences its match record leaves open. Liberty L-k01-2123-prairie-3724; review: docs/RESEARCH/k01-2123-prairie-3724/README.md.
